doc.title: Frank Wess interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 29, 1995

title: Hearing music live
summary: Live music communicates and listeners feel it as natural.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: You know this is something that one of the other musicians that we interviewed talked about. He said it’s important to hear this music live.

And the reason why I’d sort of like you to elaborate on this is, when I hear something live, I make an immediate value judgment about how that music is effecting me. When the artist finishes a piece, if I really enjoy that piece, I clap my hands. And because that music moved me, I was participating in the moment with what that person was playing or saying.

Well that’s what it’s about. It’s communication. And you feel that. And people feel that when the music is being made in front of them. It’s like watching somebody cook a dish. You know you put some of this in and some of that. And people can tell when it’s not contrived, it’s when you’re actually doing it on the spot. But people can tell that. And they enjoy that. I mean mistakes and all, they enjoy it because it’s natural.
Yeah, it’s what the creation is all about.
